paper.title: Perturbed-History Exploration in Stochastic Linear Bandits

settings.definition_quote: Let $K$ be the number of arms, $x_i \in \realset^d$ be the feature vector of arm $i \in [K]$, and $\theta_\ast \in \realset^d$ be an unknown parameter vector. The reward of arm $i$ in round $t \in [n]$, $Y_{i, t}$, is drawn i.i.d. from a distribution of that arm with mean $\mu_i = x_i\T \theta_\ast$. ... rewards are bounded in $[0, 1]$ ... the last feature is a bias term ... the feature vectors of the last $d$ arms are a basis in $\realset^d$.

algorithms.name: LinPHE (perturbed-history exploration in a linear bandit)
Any model-based algorithm (pulls argmax_i x_i^T theta_tilde_t)

bound.expression_latex: (c_1 + c_2) \left(1 + \frac{2}{p_3 - p_2}\right) \sqrt{c_3 n} + (p_1 + p_2) n + d

symbols.c_1: confidence width constant for least-squares estimate (>=1)
symbols.c_2: confidence width constant for perturbed estimate (>=1)
symbols.p_1: upper bound on probability that least-squares estimate is not close in some round
symbols.p_2: upper bound on per-round probability that the perturbed estimate is not close
symbols.p_3: lower bound on per-round probability the optimal arm's estimate is optimistic

source.label: thm:lin upper bound
source.quote: Let $c_1, c_2 \geq 1$. Let $A$ be any algorithm that pulls arm $I_t = \argmax_{i \in [K]} x_i\T \tilde{\theta}_t$ in round $t$, where $\tilde{\theta}_t$ is estimated from past data. Let the rewards be in $[0, 1]$; $p_1$, $p_2$, and $p_3$ be defined as above; and $p_3 > p_2$. Then the expected $n$-round regret of $A$ is bounded as $R(n) \leq (c_1 + c_2) (1 + \frac{2}{p_3 - p_2}) \sqrt{c_3 n} + (p_1 + p_2) n + d$

results.notes: Generic bound for any randomized model-based algorithm; the paper says it is extracted from prior work (Agrawal & Goyal 2013; Valko et al. 2014) but states it as its own theorem. Regret is defined via gaps times expected pull counts, so it is pseudo-regret. Expressed through abstract constants.

symbols.c_1: (1/2) sqrt(d log(n + n^2 L^2/(d lambda))) + lambda^{1/2} ||theta_*||

conditions: last feature is bias term; last d arms form a basis
arm 1 is the unique optimal arm

source.label: thm:linphe upper bound
source.quote: Let all parameters be chosen as in \cref{tab:constants} and $n > \max \set{34, \, 8 \sqrt{2} c_1} = \tilde{O}(d)$. Then the expected $n$-round regret of $\linphe$ is $R(n) = \tilde{O}(d \sqrt{n})$.

results.notes: The proof uses L = O(sqrt d) and ||theta_*|| = O(sqrt d). Tuning a = ceil(16 c_1^2) requires n, d, ||theta_*|| and L.
